heading ashore, then?” he summed up. The dragonslayer considered the possibilities.
Between the strength of the three of them, they should be well protected from any threat the
island could hold, short of divine beasts or any unexpected calamity. Even if there were
enemy Servants, they would be able to easily repel the attack – or at least buy time for a
withdrawal.
“Oh, uh… I should probably stay behind then, huh?”
All of them turned in surprise to see Ritsuka scratching her cheek abashedly. “You wanted to
come too, Ritsu?” Morgana asked.
The girl shrugged helplessly. “Well yeah. Hasn’t every kid wanted to go on a pirate’s treasure
hunt?” she confessed. “But it sounds like it’s a bit too risky right now, and I don’t wanna drag
Mash down by having to babysit me the entire time. I’ll just hang back, maybe ask Medea to
scry on you guys and keep tabs on your progress.”
Ren and Morgana looked at one another. “You sure you don’t wanna come with?” the former
asked in surprise. “It does seem like a pretty fun adventure, after all.”
Ritsuka hesitated, then nodded. “I’m sure,” she replied with a smile that seemed rather
forced. “If you guys can, pick up a souvenir or two for me – and for Mash too while you’re at
it. Girls do like jewelry, after all.”
The Phantom Thief stared at Ritsuka for a moment, his expression unreadable for a moment.
Then he nodded. “I’ll see what I can find,” he replied with a smile. “Just take it easy,

alright?” He reached over and gently patted her on the head.
At the contact, the girl froze in surprise, then slowly and almost reluctantly relaxed. “No
promises,” she replied with a small smile. Ren couldn’t help but give a small chuckle at his
own words being thrown right back at him.
“The landing ship is ready to go!” Mash reported as she walked up. “The captain said to
retrieve you when you’re ready.” She paused and looked between Ren and Ritsuka. “Oh, I’m
sorry. Am I interrupting?”
“We were just seeing who’s coming,” the Phantom Thief replied, withdrawing his hand. “You
ready for a treasure hunt, Mash?”
The Shielder nodded enthusiastically. “Oh yes,” she replied, beaming. “I had always been
curious about treasure hunts. While I doubt it will be as simple as following a map until we
reach the specific spot, it will be rather informative regardless. I’ve also double-checked our
supplies in case we’re stranded or require rescue, including emergency flares. Would you like
to take one, Ren-senpai?”
Ren blinked, then nodded with a grin. “Sure,” he accepted. “You’ve been getting a lot more
thorough, Mash.”
Mash turned slightly red at the compliment. “I-It’s merely what I’m supposed to do,” she
stammered slightly. Nevertheless, she smiled as she grabbed emergency flares from behind
her shield and handed one to Ren and Morgana.
Ren did his best to hide his displeasure, Mash still had a long way to go, it seemed. He could
only hope she’d grow properly into her own person, with what he could do to help. “Thanks,
Mash.”
“Oi!” Drake roared from near the boat. “You lot take any longer and I’m tossing you into the
sea so you can swim to the island! Get over here already!”
Morgana shuddered at the prospect. “Never thought we’d meet someone more impatient for
treasure than us,” he remarked. “Let’s get a move on, guys!”
Ren, Mash, and Siegfried nodded. “Catch you in a bit, Ritsu!” the former said cheerfully as
they met up with Drake.
They all boarded the landing boat – a rowboat that felt almost hilariously tiny in comparison
to the Golden Hind. While the galleon had multiple boats it could dispatch, only one would
be sent as a reconnaissance outing. Drake was about to take three of her own crew along,
mainly for mapmaking and marking a path to any treasure, but Morgana volunteered his
services.
“You can draw maps?” the captain asked skeptically.
“Don’t underestimate the first of the Phantom Thieves,” the catlike being boasted, standing
proudly despite his diminutive height.

“He was our navigator before some of our other crew joined and still worked as one when
push came to shove,” Ren piped up. And that was that.
That said, between Drake and the Chaldeans, the boat ride had been rather cramped. Siegfried
had taken to spirit form and would meet them on the shore while Morgana rode on Ren’s lap
to save on space. Joan sat across from Ren and was pointedly looking away, their frosty
silence and distance palpable to everyone on board. Mash, who was sitting beside Ren
glanced at him questioningly, and he simply smiled ruefully and shook his head in reply.
Rowing through the waves, they eventually beached on the shore. As Siegfried materialized
and hauled the boat out of the water, Drake scanned the tree line beyond and took a large
breath. “Nothing like the smell of loam and bark when you’ve been on the sea for so long,”
she remarked with a grin before turning to the others. “Come on, you sluggards! We’re gonna
haul some treasure back before this day is done!"
“Think you can sense any treasure around here?” Ren asked his best friend with an amused
smirk.
Morgana chuckled as Siegfried finished hauling the boat well onto the shore. “The captain’s
got sharp senses, I gotta admit – I smell treasure too,” he replied. “This is shaping up to be a
fruitful expedition. Keep on your toes though – where there’s treasure, there’s bound to be
danger.”
“Wouldn’t be much of an adventure without some,” the Phantom Thief agreed with a grin. He
looked up at Mash and Siegfried. “You guys ready as well?”
“Yes, senpai!” Mash chirped.
“I am at your disposal,” the dragonslayer replied smiling.
“I’ll take point,” Joan suddenly growled out. Without waiting for a response, she marched off
ahead of the others to join Drake up in front.
Morgana stared at her marching off, then looked over at Ren. “What happened?” he asked.
The Phantom Thief sighed. “… We got something worked out,” he answered with a rueful
smile. “Come on, before the captain gets impatient and has us walk the plank.”
“That’s if I’m in a good mood!” Drake called back with a broad grin. “I can get more creative
– and not finding treasure before dusk is gonna put me in a bad one! So get a damn move
on!” The Chaldeans looked at one another, chuckled, then entered the forest right behind the
captain and Joan.
As the sand gave way to soil and the foliage enveloped them, the atmosphere changed. The
forest was teeming with life, from the chirps of birds to the fluttering of insect wings. There
wasn’t much on the ground, allowing them surprisingly easy traversal. While the temperature
was balmy, it was also surprisingly humid, leaving the air stickier than any of them were
comfortable with.

“At least the Master uniforms have decent aeration,” Ren commented, tugging at his sleeve
idly.
“There’s worse,” Morgana replied without looking up from the map he was sketching on a
piece of paper given to him by Mash. “The jungle where we hunted that bat was way worse –
lots more plants to the point I couldn’t even walk and had to ride on Boudica’s shoulder, and
it was so humid that my fur was practically sticking. At least Medea had some magecraft to
make it more reasonable for me.”
“Medea does seem a woman of much knowledge,” Mash mused. “Perhaps I should talk with
her myself and see if I could learn from her.”
“I wouldn’t try that if I were you,” the catlike being warned, shooting a glance at the Shielder
before checking his compass. “She’s already warned me against trying to learn her stuff and
probably won’t appreciate being bothered for that.”
“Ah. That’s a shame,” Mash demurred, her shoulders sagging slightly in disappointment.
‘That said,’ Morgana continued, mentally contacting Ren. ‘I managed to convince her to help
me but let me tell you, it was like pulling teeth.’
That got Ren’s curiosity. ‘What are you learning from her?’ he asked, resisting the urge to
look down at his best friend.
‘When I mentioned to her about my transformations, she got very interested,’ Morgana
elaborated. ‘She had me work on assembling models together. Said it was to change my
perception of my body? I don’t quite get it yet, but I’m still working at it.’
The catlike being paused. ‘And I won’t lie, it’s kinda fun,’ he sheepishly admitted. ‘It’s been a
while since I was able to work with my paws ever since Tokyo. Not quite like making
lockpicks or smoke bombs, but it’s still pretty nice.’
Ren couldn’t help but smile. ‘It has been a while hasn’t it?’ he mused. ‘In that case, I look
forward to what you’ll learn from Medea. Knowing her, it’s bound to be great.’
Morgana blinked, then puffed himself up slightly. ‘Once we get to the good stuff, you bet it
will be,’ he confirmed confidently. ‘Leave it to me, Joker – the great Morgana will be more
awesome than ever in no time at all!’
As they trekked further, the land slowly rose uphill until it became more of a hike than a
walk. The loose soil made their footing less steady than any of them liked, but hardly
untraversable. There was the occasional sound of leaves rustling and twigs breaking as a
distant animal moved, but nothing visible. Ren occasionally scanned around them with his
Third Eye but nothing of note appeared in his sight, neither hostile nor any signs of treasure.
Yet.
“Are you seeing anything in particular, senpai?” Mash asked.

The Phantom Thief shook his head as his eyes returned to normal. “Nothing so far,” he
replied. “It’s been pretty quiet. Only thing I can see so far are all the plants around us –
though they’re pretty interesting. They remind me of the ones we saw during the Roman
singularity.”
“Oh, you’ve noticed too?” Mash chirped, beaming. “I looked into the plant life of the
Mediterranean after we got back from Chaldea. I figured it was a good idea after…” Then her
eyes widened and she turned away, embarrassed.
“After what?” Ren asked, looking over in curiosity.
“… after you were poisoned that one time,” she whispered. “The doctor told me you had
been poisoned with belladonna berries. I thought it would be a good idea to do some research
afterward in the toxicology of belladonna and… it expanded into the horticulture of the
Mediterranean. It was an interesting line of research, though I wasn’t sure how much of it is
applicable here..."
“Why wouldn’t it be?” the Phantom Thief countered, to the Shielder’s surprise. “If a lot of
the plants around here are located around the Mediterranean, then I’d say it’s plenty
applicable. Anything you can tell me about the plant life around here? Might lead to some
clues that we could use.”
Mash’s eyes widened, then glittered in delight. Immediately she launched into a recitation of
what she learned – the prevalence of broadleaf trees that compose the forests, primarily oak
which was the sacred tree of Zeus, as well as pine and walnut. The thick shrubbery all around
them that went by different names like phrygana in Greece. Various herbs that had medicinal
properties, such as the common chamomile and the red valerian, and even for cooking such
as sage and fennel.
Ren smiled as he listened to Mash continuing to list different species of plants around them
from what she had studied. He knew she had been working hard in her own right, through
both her own studies and her training with Leonidas. He was eager to see what she would
become in the future – undoubtedly she had the potential to be as grand as the Servants they
fought alongside.
Then his eyes rested on something – a bunch of yellow flowers growing nearby. Before he
knew it, he found himself kneeling next to them, a finger gently lifting a petal.
“Are you curious about that flower, senpai?” Mash asked. Morgana and Siegfried were
behind her, looking over curiously before the latter caught up with Joan and Drake to talk to
them.
The Phantom Thief opened his mouth to answer, then reconsidered. “Not… curious – at least,
not in that sense,” he replied with a wry smile. “I know this little guy – the common
snapdragon. In flower language, it means deception and graciousness.”
The Shielder blinked in surprise. “Kind of like you, senpai!” she chirped.

“You think so?” Ren laughed. “Yellow’s not really my color though – it suits my friend Ryuji
a lot more, if you ask me. I used to sell them back in Tokyo, along with other flowers. You’d
be surprised at what people ask me to make for them.”
Mash tilted her head. “Do they not simply ask for a bouquet?” she asked. She only heard of
flowers being sold in passing, either individually as a more romantic gesture or in bouquets
for either congratulatory or an even greater romantic reason.
“A few do,” Ren confirmed. “But most want one for specific reasons – to congratulate
someone for a promotion or a new job, to celebrate a baby’s new birth, or the ever-classic
Valentine’s or to bring to a date or loved one. Aside from aesthetics – which are incredibly
important, don’t get me wrong – the flowers chosen could also convey a certain meaning
when bundled together. Most of them are touching messages, of course, though once or twice
I put together bundles that I’m pretty sure were insults.”
The Shielder’s eyes widened. “That’s terrible!” she gasped, taken aback. “Why would they
do such a thing?”
The Phantom Thief shrugged. “Who knows?” he replied. “Everyone has their own reasons
for what they do or what they want. And if that’s what they want, then who am I to restrict
them? So long as they’re aware of what they’re doing and know the consequences, then all I
can do is send the flowers off with a smile. The flowers never really hurt anyone intentionally
anyway.”
Mash hesitated. “And… what if they’re not aware?” she asked softly.
“I try my best to let them know,” Ren answered with a now thinner, yet still wry smile.
“Thankfully a few customers get my subtle hints before going too far. The ones who are
deliberate… well, not much I can do about that.”
“… I didn’t realize that selling flowers had such complexities,” the girl mused.
“Well, that’s the exception rather than the norm,” he reassured her. “Besides, it’s not so bad –
you get to chat with people from all walks of life. A guy trying to confess properly for the
first time. A sister celebrating her brother’s marriage. Grandparents who are about to witness
their grandchild be born. They’re about as plentiful, different, and vividly colored as all the
flowers in the store. I rarely got bored.”
As the Phantom Thief spoke about them, he could recollect each customer fairly clearly in his
mind, which was odd – under normal circumstances, their faces would be indistinct to him.
Just people he met among the dozens of customers he had when he worked at the flower
shop. They all had their own stories, sure, but it would’ve quickly been buried among all his
other experiences.
But now? Now they stood out so clearly to him. Was it just because of this flower? Was it
because he had recollected the story to Mash that he remembered it so clearly? Or was it
simply because they were all gone – just like every single person in the world aside from
Chaldea? His senior coworker, Suzuka, said she was going to America with her boyfriend
over the summer. He wondered if they had a good time.

“Perhaps I should work at a flower shop myself,” Mash idly mused. “It definitely sounds
rather informative.”
“Heh, maybe,” Ren agreed. It was easy to imagine her as a flower shop clerk. Her lilac hair
would even be a good match for it too. Perhaps once the world was brought back, that could
be something she could explore for herself. It would certainly be a great way for her to
experience the world and meet all sorts of people like he had.
His smile slowly vanished from his face as he contemplated. He had already dedicated
himself to the Grand Order so he could bring the whole world back. But the more he thought
about it, the more overwhelming the mission seemed. Just the two main singularities they had
been on had been monstrous: The Dragon Witch and the devastation of France, and the
United Roman Empire and their countless armies. And those were the easier ones. That
didn’t include the hunts and that odd singularity of Elizabeth’s.
It all just rubbed in his face that, despite saving Tokyo and taking down both Yaldabaoth and
Maruki, there was so much he lacked. When he had been slow to recover at the start, what he
had done to Joan, his failings with Ritsuka and Mash, when he had been too slow to save that
soldier from bleeding out… he could have been – should have been – faster, stronger, more
intelligent about it all. There were other ways he could’ve handled himself and make them all
stronger.
Yet he didn’t. Time and time again, he had failed. And there was still much to go. How many
singularities would there be left? How many more mistakes would he make? How many of
those would he even be able to recover from? He had saved Tokyo before – twice, even –
through a combination of his friends, happenstance, and his own burgeoning skills. Would
that be enough here? Would anything be enough?
While he didn’t have an answer, he only knew that he would never stop. That understanding
coiled around his heart like an icy serpent. It was a sinking, crushing kind of determination he
had only felt once before: When he woke on the floor of the Velvet Room after he and his
team had their existences erased – the result of their first assault into the depths of Mementos.
Everything he was currently doing might just be the pointless flailing of a dying animal, yet
that didn’t stop him in the least. Running on spite and defiance wasn’t a perfect substitute for
hope, but it was motivation all the same.
“Senpai…?” Mash asked, watching him in concern as his mood slowly shifted and became
gloomy. “Is something the matter?”
“Oh, just reflecting on when I’ll get to see those people again,” the Phantom Thief replied
with a humorless smile. His eyes turned up to the sky. The now sunny weather now seemed
to be mocking him with its brightness and cheer. “Just getting the sinking feeling it’ll be quite
a while is all.” His words were murmured more than spoken, as though he was saying it more
to himself in resignation than to answer her.
Mash swallowed as she observed Ren’s face with growing concern. The furrows in his brow,
his cynical, biting tone, and most importantly, his smile. Normally it held such warmth and
friendliness, it didn’t reach his eyes and was cold to witness. She had seen him weather

through harsher situations with a laugh and a smirk. It heartened and encouraged her. What
she saw now, that expression on her senpai’s face… this wasn’t him at all.
She could not let this stand.
“It won’t be, senpai,” the Shielder denied. Her tone carried such vehemence that the young
man turned to her in surprise. “We will bring everyone back – and sooner rather than later. It
may be difficult and the path is long, but it can and will be done! And if I must push myself
even harder to become the kind of Servant needed, then I will!”
Ren could only blink several times at Mash’s sudden outburst. Slowly, a smile spread across
his lips as a weight lifted off his shoulders. “Yeah, you’re right,” he agreed quietly. “Thanks,
Mash. That… that means a lot to me.”
The Shielder froze momentarily at the sight of his smile. “O-of course, senpai,” she
stammered slightly. “Just… I meant what I said. Both that we’ll get everyone back and I’ll do
my best to be even better – both to protect you and to fulfill our mission.”
“I know,” the Phantom Thief replied. “Just don’t push yourself too hard, alright? You’re
already doing a lot as is, and I’m more than grateful for all of it.”
“I won’t,” Mash promised with a cheerful smile of her own, widening Ren’s own in turn.
“OI!!” came a sudden irritated shout from Drake through the forest, causing both of them to
jump. “Are you two gonna pick flowers all day or are we gonna get a move on?!?”
Ren chuckled as he stood back up, brushing the dirt off his knees. “Come on,” he said. “We
better get going before Drake actually has us walk the plank.”
“I’m not sure her mood is good enough for that,” Mash noted as she stood up as well.
“Hm, true,” the Phantom Thief agreed as he rubbed his chin thoughtfully. “Maybe tie us to a
mast and use us for target practice?”
“I believe there’s an old practice of cutting pieces of flesh to use as fish bait,” the Shielder
added as they walked to catch up with her.
They both walked away, brainstorming methods that Drake would punish them. All the
while, the snapdragon flowers simply swayed with a gentle breeze, caring for little around it
save for the glowing afternoon sun.
“I can practically smell treasure down there,” Drake remarked, grinning hungrily.
“I’m practically smelling the danger down there,” Joan deadpanned.
The group had found a cave that led straight down. Sunlight filtered down and vanished into
its depths, leaving only darkness below. Around them, the trees had given way to a rocky
slope that gently rode until a sheer cliff a small distance away loomed over them. Other than
that, the cave seemed almost entirely ordinary.

Morgana took a sniff as his ears twitched. “Odd. I’m not hearing or smelling any bats,” he
noticed.
“Maybe they’re just farther in?” Mash suggested.
“Mash, believe me, after that hunt and all those bats, I couldn’t forget how the sounds or
smells even if I wanted to,” he shot back, shuddering with recollection. “No, I’m not even
catching a whiff or a squeak from them down there. If the cave’s empty, then there would be
bats nesting but if there isn’t… there’s probably something else in there.”
“Probably a bear or something of the sort,” the captain brushed off, then grinned. “Or maybe
a bigger creature. Think their bones and hide would sell for a lot?”
“Even during my time, dragon parts were quite valuable commodities,” Siegfried commented
as he crossed his arms. “The scales and hide made for surprisingly sturdy armor, the bones
were good for reconstruction material, and I believe its sinew and organs found much use
among the druids and wise men we had among us.”
“You would definitely know,” the captain replied with a smug grin. “Alright then! We’re
going in!” As she spoke, she reached into her coat and pulled out a rope that she wrapped
around a nearby tree, as well as a small lantern that she lit up.
“Where the heck did you keep all that?!” Morgana spouted in surprise as he looked up and
down Drake’s light clothing.
“Ain’t no sailor worth their salt that don’t have rope and a lantern wherever they’re needed

Before anyone could object, she was already climbing down into the cavern with surprising
dexterity and speed.
Ren couldn’t help but laugh in amusement. “She does have a point,” he agreed. “So, who
wants to head down next?”
“Please, allow me, senpai,” Mash piped up. “I’ll make sure the area is secure before you
come down.”
“Sounds good,” the Phantom Thief easily agreed. “Siegfried, mind being rearguard?”
“Of course,” the dragonslayer immediately concurred.
Ren turned around to Joan and hesitated for a moment. “Joan-“ he began to say.
“I’ll head down right after Mash,” she growled, staring down in the cavern like it had

The Phantom Thief closed his mouth, then nodded. “Appreciate it,” he replied.
With the order decided, Ren turned back down to the cavern and saw the glimmer of Drake’s
lantern. “How’s it looking down there?” he called, hearing his voice echo.

“Empty and dark!” the captain’s raucous voice called back immediately. “I see a passageway
though! Let’s go!”
The Phantom Thief nodded and glanced at the others. They began climbing down one at a
time in the order described, with Morgana hopping on Ren’s shoulder as he climbed down

Once Ren reached the ground, he took the flashlight out of his pocket and clicked it on. Now

“Ugh, this place stinks,” Morgana complained, holding a paw of his nose. “No bats, but I

Siegfried appeared with a shower of golden light and took a small sniff in response. “Long

“Wyverns,” Joan growled out, her grip on her sword tightening. “We should get out of here.
Now.”
“Are you all so lily-livered?” Drake spat. “I thought you two were warriors. How the hell is a
privateer braver than either of you? I brought you lot here for this exact reason – there’s no
reward without risk, as they say, and if this place is as dangerous as you say, then there’s
definitely something here we can work with. So no, we ain’t bailin’. If you are, then find

The Lancer turned around to glare daggers at her. “You are dragging us into an enormous risk
for the sake of your greed,” she snarled.
“And what of it?” the captain spat back, easily meeting the Lancer’s rage with an impetuous
stare of her own.
The hostility between the two women was quickly growing thicker as the captain’s hand
wandered toward her pistols – then Ren suddenly popped up between them. “I understand the
concern,” he quickly said. “But this is a treasure hunt – sometimes we can get lost in the
moment, especially when we’re getting relatively close. With treasure hunts come danger –
it’s part and parcel of the whole deal, after all.”
Joan’s displeasure quickly morphed into a snarl. Before she could retort, however, Ren
continued. “That said, Joan has a point,” he added. “We shouldn’t take unnecessary risks for
treasure here. After all, you can’t really enjoy the treasure if you’re too dead for it.” Drake
paused, then nodded in agreement after a moment of consideration.

The Phantom Thief turned to the Lancer. “What do you suggest, Joan?” he asked.
The woman in question looked around her, scowling in distaste both at having to make a call
and the all-too-familiar scents and sights of the environment around her. “I’ll stay here for

from behind and catching us off guard – or cutting off our retreat.
Ren nodded in response and tossed her his flashlight, which she deftly caught in surprise.
“Thanks, Joan,” he replied with genuine gratefulness, to which she simply grunted slightly in

Drake stared down at him for a moment with a satisfied smile. “You’re alright, Joker,” she

“Hope whatever we find is worth it,” Morgana whispered on Ren’s shoulder as he quietly

The Phantom Thief chortled in amusement as he followed the captain. “Didn’t think you’d be
the one to pass up on treasure,” he quipped.
“I’m not,” his best friend shot back. “But… ugh. Wyverns. And underground too.”
“I’m sure we’ll be able to handle it,” Ren reassured him. “Right, Mash?”
“Huh?” Mash started. “Of course, senpai. I will keep you both safe. I swear it.”
“As will I,” came Siegfried’s measured response as he gave a small smile. Ren grinned in
response.
They marched on through the caves, their footsteps echoing along the strong walls and
ceilings. Drake was in the lead, marching confidently with her lantern held high as her alert,
experienced eyes quickly took in her surroundings for threats and treasure. Mash was right
behind her, shield in hand as her eyes darted about, alert for any wyverns. Ren followed
behind with Morgana still perched on his shoulder, his eyes blood red as this Third Eye took
in any and every detail possible. Siegfried brought up the rear, occasionally glancing behind
him in case they were pursued.
Before too long, they stopped at their first obstacle: a cliff face. It wasn’t too high – they
could easily see the top – but it was far too tall for a regular person to jump, and it was sheer
enough that simply climbing it wasn’t an option. As Drake fished out another length of rope
from her coat, Ren glanced at Siegfried. “Mind checking the top and making sure it’s all
clear?” he asked.
The dragonslayer nodded. Vanishing into a shower of golden light, he easily made his way to
the top and solidified himself out of spirit form once again, his eyes quickly checking the
surroundings. All he could see was a corridor that led further ahead. However, though the
scent of fire and venom was fainter, he could see more claw marks along the stone walls and

the cave’s stalactites and stalagmites. The tunnel was dragon made, but there were no
immediate threats he could register.
‘More claw marks here, but nothing that currently indicates the presence of wyverns in the
vicinity,’ the Saber mentally reported to Ren and Morgana. ‘All clear, Master.’
Ren nodded in response as Drake glanced over. “How’s it lookin’, Joker?” she asked.
“We’re good for now,” he replied before nodding to the rope. “Want me to take that up
there?” he asked.
Drake raised an eyebrow. “Think your doodad can get up there?” she inquired, nodding to the
Phantom Thief’s wrist where the grappling hook was still strapped on.
Ren grinned. “Time to find out,” he cheekily replied. Raising his arm, he expertly fired up at
one of the more solid-looking stalagmites standing near the edge of the cliff. It wrapped
around easily and secured itself before beginning to reel the Phantom Thief in. Taking the
rope from Drake, he jumped and allowed it to pull him up, rapidly up the cliff and reaching
the top, where Siegfried patiently awaited him. Withdrawing the hook, he tied the rope
around the selfsame stalagmite before tossing the length of the edge to the women waiting

The caverns were surprisingly direct. Aside from one or two forks, all of which led to dead

Even with the enchantments of the Chaldean Master uniform, Ren could feel his own limbs

The corridor had opened up into an enormous chamber. The air had become far cooler though

Occasionally they shifted, the sound of their scales scraping against rock and the skin of their
wings rustling causing their hearts to stop momentarily before quiet fell once more.

Then the rope shook, causing all three of them to freeze. Something was pulling on the other

That’s what he told them, anyway.

Business as usual.
Archer was highly accustomed to dirty work. His duties as a counter guardian often meant
massacring countless people and threats to humanity - often a grisly fate for both him and his
victims alike. Collateral damage had been acceptable… and unavoidable. The bodies of

innocent and guilty alike piled high underneath him as he carried out his grim task, staining
his hands with their blood. And there was always a threat to humanity, leaving him no
reprieve.
Still, at the end of the day, hanging up his sword and bow was simply never an option for
him, no matter how much he begged for it in his heart. He had killed, he killed, and he would
kill again. That was the simple truth of who he was.
In comparison, his duties in Chaldea were considerably lighter. Allies he worked with
towards a common goal of preserving both the world and humanity, enemies that he had no
remorse or regrets about taking down, and their definition of ‘dirty work’ was far lighter in
comparison. Despite himself, there was a lightness in his heart he hadn’t felt in a very long
time – one that filled him with bitterness and amusement in equal measure.
His foolish past self would’ve loved this place.
“Artemis is settling down,” the red-mantled hero casually reported as he stepped into the
command room. “She took one of the rooms nearby the Graveyard wing – she seems to
prefer the quiet there compared to the main living quarters.” He had been chosen to be the
goddess’s chaperone in a tour of Chaldea as well as getting her set up – mainly so he could
keep an eye on her in case something went amiss or she threw yet another tantrum. For the
most part, however, it went smoothly, if a bit nauseating.
The displays of affection between Artemis and Orion weren’t things he was used to.
His report was met with a distracted silence as everyone stared at their monitors, with both
Da Vinci and Roman focusing on the central displays. It didn’t take much for him to guess
what had happened. “I take it our Masters have found themselves in trouble yet again?” he
drawled as he continued walking over.
Despite the casualness of his tone, his steel-grey eyes were already scanning the information
shown on the display and quickly piecing together the increasingly grim nature of the
situation at hand. If there was one thing his foolish past self and his current Masters had in
common, it was how they always seemed to be a magnet for trouble.
“You could say that,” Da Vinci answered with a forced lightness and smile. “The island they
had explored turned out to be a rather massive wyvern’s nest – and they managed to wake all

been… difficult.”

“No doubt,” Archer murmured as he glanced over at the map – and saw something

concerningly. Can we get into contact with him?”

His breath came out in ragged gasps as he ran. His heartbeat was loud in his ear. The cool

And behind him, above everything he currently heard or experienced, were the growls and

So he kept running. Past what used to be the forest they had walked through, now uprooted

Every time he slowed down even slightly meant his pursuers were gaining on him. Even at

Soil began giving way to sand. Through the treeline, he could see swarms of wyverns

After what felt like an eternity passed, it all stopped. With an almost unconscious groan, he

And most importantly, to his horror, the boat was completely missing from the shore. It only

Cybele.
The beautiful, horned, blue-skinned woman came forth once more in a burst of flame. With a
seductive smile, she pointed at Ren, causing him to glow green once more. The sharp pain
within his body rapidly diminished, replaced instead by his circuits scalding his flesh again

stamina flagged dangerously as he withstood the burning of his circuits. Then a moment later,
his persona vanished, allowing him a bit of reprieve from it all.
He reflexively touched his stomach and let out a small, humorless chuckle. It was still better
than the Bake-Kujira’s rotten water, at least.

The effect was subtle at first. It tasted warm and oddly spicy to his tongue, yet not enough to

He stood back up, shaking some seawater from his clothes and rolling his neck as he took a

He inhaled, and time slowed. He could hear the lapping of waves around him, splashing

High above, the late afternoon sun bore down on him, warming the soaked clothes plastered

“Right,” the Phantom Thief breathed as he slid underneath a fallen tree trunk and continued

The energy from the potion was rapidly waning. His muscles ached with the strain he was

a distance he had traveled at this point and for how long – all he had focused on was solely

Not that he dared to consider slowing down, regardless of any consequences, the visions

Joan's complicated glare, Olga's exhausted analysis, Mash's hopeful determination, and the

Finally, a light broke through, and he saw the sky ahead. The ground below ended abruptly,
as though he had reached the very end of the world.
It was now or never.
His muddled mind put together the pieces of the puzzle in his head as the finale rapidly
approached. He didn’t have the magical energy left to create a full persona, so he had only

one choice. To create a projection, first came the chant. He wasted no time on consideration,

‘Masks of my soul…’
Then he broke out of the forest as the spell primed, what little ground he had left providing

in his legs, drew upon his magecraft,
And leaped.
For a small, infinite moment, it felt like he was utterly weightless. His legs churned

sparkling filigree of gems, marked only by the dark shape of the Golden Hind in the distance.
At the moment, it was perhaps the most beautiful scene he had ever seen.
Then in the next instant, he fell. His heart jumped to his throat as he rapidly descended.
Below were the rocks at the base of the cliff jutting out of the surf - cold, merciless monoliths
that would dash his life, as inevitable as fate.
And yet, his only answer was to close his eyes. He focused inward, fractions of a second
stretching as his world dwindled to merely his own existence.
Gazing at himself with his Third Eye wasn’t something he tried before, but he recalled the
basics of structural analysis he had been taught. It was a similar concept, if a different
execution. As he observed himself, every proportion of his physical body painted themselves
upon his mind as if they were the factors in a computer’s equation.
He focused upon his back. His spine was stretched almost perfectly vertical by his falling.
His muscles and ligaments tensed, bracing him futilely for a landing of certain death. The
veins and arteries that fed blood across his being, supplying his sinews with vital nutrients
and oxygen.
He focused on his truest other self, the demonized phantom thief of myth and renown. But
not the whole like he had always done before. Instead, he narrowed it down to the imposing,
iridescent wonder of his jet-black raven wings. As he focused, it felt like all the other aspects
of Arsene - his body, his claws, his burning grin - vanished from existence, leaving only the
shadowed wings.
As he plummeted, the wind buffeted his body with a deafening force as his end raced up to
meet him. He allowed the images to overlap in his mind, letting the looming threat of
imminent death narrow all that he was into the image being carved into his subconscious. A
solitary image, almost greater than anything he had portrayed before.
That he too, could break the shackles of the world and take to the skies.
‘… Become my wings of rebellion!!’

Suddenly, an odd sensation gripped him: A shiver ran through his body as Arsene’s laugh

vision with blue and black. Taking a deep breath, he willed his new limbs to moveAnd his stomach lurched as his descent quickly slowed into a glide, then steadied out, and
finally he was drifting a foot above the ocean surface. He looked down in wonder at the

glance back, his eyes widened as he saw Arsene’s wings attached to him, easily keeping him
level as he flew. A certain emotion began bubbling within him like a wellspring, but before it
could completely take hold‘HAHAHAHAHAHA!!!!’ Cu Chulainn howled over the communicator. ‘You did it, kid! Ya

Flapping his newfound wings, he began gaining some altitude. He thought they would take

With an excited cry, he immediately began experimenting with his newfound flight: Pulling

fluttering through his wings. He didn’t just feel alive – he felt completely and utterly free.
Free to go where he wished whenever and however he wanted, not bound by the constraints
of society and certainly not gravity. He felt like he could soar to the ends of the earth and
beyond.

He always did.
Mash’s wide eyes stared as Ritsuka almost ran away, then turned back to look at her Master.

Yet what about her? Why wasn’t she there?
The tropical air around her chilled. Her senpai had always been there for her. He had offered
her his hand back when Chaldea was bombed instead of escaping. He had respected her

She clenched her hand on its grip so hard that her knuckles turned white as the metal
underneath the wrap dug painfully into her palm. The Chimera would’ve been the perfect
target for her new blade, and yet it had remained sheathed and unused the whole time. There

Chimera was too strong to justify something new as opposed to her more practiced
techniques, the shield was more useful for the circumstance – but even those half-hearted

Her senpai had survived – not because he made excuses or stuck with what he knew, but
because he took yet another step forward into the unknown. He had pushed himself beyond
all his limitations once again, forming wings and flying to safety. Mash hadn’t heard even a
whisper of the method from him whenever she came across him during his magecraft studies.
In fact, she wasn’t even sure either he or El-Melloi ever even thought up of it.

Yet here he was, his great black wings testifying to his willingness to embrace risk for the

Despite that, something within her stirred. That silent howling deep within her that may have

Mash cast one last glance at the Phantom Thief. I’m very glad you’re okay, senpai, she

She would have the opportunity to check up on him later. Perhaps a veteran warrior like
Siegfried might have some insight on what to do going forward. She made a mental note to

For now, she turned and followed Ritsuka’s path. There was indeed much to do on a ship,

trusted betrayed them both and tormented her for years after his death. It was a slight he
couldn’t possibly forgive nor forget. The dragonslayer never believed himself the most noble
of men, but he understood now how some burned with unyielding vengeance and hatred. If
he ever encountered that man again…
“Seems like she has good taste,” the Phantom Thief remarked with a yawn. “Kinda wanna
fall asleep here. It’s a nice evening for it.”
… And suddenly, with that one flippant comment, all his darker thoughts vanished like a puff
of smoke. His Master’s lightheartedness was a balm he hadn’t realized he needed, but he
certainly appreciated it. “While understandable, I’d advise against sleeping on the deck of a
ship,” the Saber cautioned with a smile. “With this many sailors moving to and fro hauling
equipment, it would be difficult to get any modicum of rest.”

Ren scoffed lightly. “Can’t be any worse than sleeping during class,” he muttered as his
eyelids drooped. “Especially with a teacher who’d throw a piece of chalk at your head if he
caught you.”
Siegfried chuckled at the remark. “I shall take your word for it then,” he easily accepted.
Glancing over, his eyes gazed in curiosity at the Phantom Thief’s wings. “I will say though,
these new appendages you have manifested are surprisingly robust,” he commented. “I’ve
seen monsters with similar wings myself. However, yours are far more pleasant: very soft to
the touch, and smooth as well. I’m reminded more of an owl’s wings rather than the plumage
of a crow.”
His Master broke into a grin as he opened one eye back up. “That’s a weird way to flirt,
Saber,” he shot back. “Don’t you know it’s not a good thing to do with people who aren’t in
their right minds at the moment? Didn’t think you were that type of guy.”
Siegfried truly laughed this time, a loud and boisterous sound that echoed far over the ocean.
“I ask for your forgiveness,” he apologized. “That wasn’t my intention.” Then an idea snuck
into his mind – no doubt the influence of his rather affable Master - and his soft smile slowly
twisted upward into something almost resembling a smirk.
“Although, I feel I must comment,” Siegfried continued, glancing down at the Phantom Thief
who had been settling against his chest and drawing a curious look from him. “Your words
and behavior don’t match someone who might take issue with such courtship. One must
forgive a humble Servant for mistaking your intention.”
Ren laughed again as well, reclining against the Saber’s arm as the dragonslayer kept a
secure hold to prevent him from falling over from exhaustion. Staring up at the darkening sky
and seeing the first glimmer of stars, he smiled warmly as his eyes closed. “Yep, she
definitely had good taste,” he conclusively stated.
The Saber smiled back as he rested against the mast as well, silently renewing his oath when
he had been summoned. His Masters were good people. His strength and his blade would
ever anon be at their service, now and in the future. Whatever battles they faced, he would be
more than glad to fight on their behalf.
And so the Golden Hind sailed onward, catching the breeze and drifting into the sunset,
where the next adventure awaited them.
