“Land ho! Land ho!”
The clamor of a bell accompanied David’s cry as it rang over the Golden Hind. The mood of
the ship picked up as everyone redoubled their pace. The morning sun was well over the
horizon and beginning its upward climb, the sea gleaming a bright turquoise in its golden
rays. A few clouds dotted the skies, but nothing like the storm that assailed them when they
first set out. It was a beautiful morning.
Drake stepped forward to the prow of the ship, taking out her spyglass from the depths of her
coat and putting it to her eye. A smile curled her lips as she spotted the telltale lightness of
land in the far distance. “Alright, put your backs into it!” she roared, turning back to the rest
of the crew. “We got a new day ahead of us! I wanna be at that island before lunch! Unfurl
the sails and catch the wind – it’s at our backs! Hop to!”
“Aye aye!” the crew chorused as they threw themselves into their work.
Ritsuka slowly rolled her neck, wincing slightly as she worked out the stiffness. Sleeping in
hammocks had been fun at first, but now she found herself missing her bed back in Chaldea,
and maybe some more scenery than just open waters. She didn’t bother voicing her
complaints though – since they weren’t getting much closer to resolving the singularity, they
would be on the seas for at least a while longer.
She glanced over to Mash, the sea breeze tussling her short pink hair as her violet eyes
gleamed with eagerness in the morning light. Back when they first met, the Shielder was
courteous and gentle, but there had been a hollowness to her she couldn’t place. How much
she had grown since then. Just this was almost enough to make waking up worth it.
Mash looked over, then blinked in surprise. “Ritsu-senpai? Is something the matter?” she
asked.
The redhead’s eyes widened slightly, then she rapidly shook her head. “Nah,” she quickly
denied. “Just thought today was going to be a good day, was all. Especially seeing how cute
you looked, Mashumallow.”

The Shielder blinked again several times, nonplussed. “Well… thank you, I guess?” she
squeaked slightly. “Did you sleep well?”
Ritsuka sighed, sagging exaggeratedly. “Man, I used to think hammocks were awesome,” she
groaned. “I always wanted to sleep in one. But now I think I’ve had my fill – I’m sore and
stiff all over, and the rocking of the ship isn’t doing me any favors either. I don’t think a
pirate’s life is for me, after all.”
Mash smiled sympathetically. “It is rather hard to get used to,” she admitted as she looked out
over the ocean. “But at least we get a rather beautiful sight to greet us, wouldn’t you agree?
The sea breeze is rather refreshing too.”
“Hrm, good point,” the redhead agreed as she joined her friend at the railing, staring out at
the beauty of the sea and breathing in the briny air. “Only thing missing is a cup of coffee
now. A little pick-me-up coupled with this scenery would be heavenly.”
“Ask and ye shall receive!” came a familiar bombastic voice. Both girls turned to see Ren
walking toward them, steaming mugs in his hands. “I figured we could all use something in
the morning, especially with a new island coming up. Here – careful, it’s hot.”
Ritsuka grinned as she accepted her mug. “You really know how to spoil a girl, don’t you,
Ren?” she remarked playfully. She took a sip – and winced as the scalding liquid hit her
tongue. “Ugh. Instant.”
The Phantom Thief nodded sadly. “Yep,” he confirmed. “Regular coffee beans would go
quickly go bad in this climate anyway. I tried at least a few tricks to make it more palatable
but I don’t exactly have much to work with.”
“It’s fine, senpai,” Mash reassured him with a bright smile. “We’re simply glad you took the
time to prepare something for us.”
Taking another sip, she stared over the ocean again. “What do you think is on the new
island?” she idly wondered.
“Hopefully not more wyverns,” Morgana grumbled as he strode up in his Metaverse form,
hopping up onto the railing and stretching. “From the France singularity and that island, I
think I’ve had enough of them for about a lifetime.”
“Oh, so you can deal with them for eight more then,” Ritsuka joked with a broad grin.
The catlike being bristled as Ren held back a chuckle at his friend’s expense. “I’m good for
all my lifetimes, thank you very much,” he snapped before his expression became pensive.
“Well, we know these islands are protected, though we only really triggered everything after

“So it could be the same, or it could be something different entirely,” Ren replied. “We were

“Perhaps the ‘keys’ disabled the protections?” Mash suggested. “They were the reason why
you even managed to find the treasure, were they not?”
“Probably, but we can’t count on that,” Ritsuka mused. “We’ve only a sample size of one so

“Good point,” the Phantom Thief acknowledged. “I’ll check in with Medea, see if she can

“Wait, hold on, ‘us’?” Morgana interjected indignantly. “Joker, you’re in no condition to head

Ren waved his concerns off as sipped at his own coffee. “I’m fine, I’m fine,” he dismissed.
“A good night’s sleep and a few stretches are all I need. It’d be nice if I had another one of

what to expect, so-“
Suddenly a hand smacked him hard on the back, causing him to yelp in surprise and pain as

The Phantom Thief winced as he slowly straightened up, his hand stinging from holding the

“In that case, I’ll stay too,” Morgana declared. “If I leave you alone, Joker, you’d just go and
find something else to do instead. I’ll make sure you get the proper rest.”
Ren gave a half-amused, half-exasperated smile to his best friend. “You’re doing that again,
Morgana?” he complained jokingly. “I thought we were well past that at this point.”
“Not when you’re like this, you’re not,” Morgana shot back, his paws on his hips. “If I gotta
be the one to tell you to sleep again, then I will.”
Mash blinked owlishly. “Again?” she echoed as she glanced up at Ren in curiosity. “Has he
told you to rest often?”
The Phantom Thief chuckled. “Back when we were in Tokyo and we had just met,” he
explained. “Morgana always made sure I went to bed on time. Didn’t matter if I had a rental
video due the next day or that I wanted to make some tools to prep for a heist – he was

The catlike being bristled again. “Joker, fighting a boss that you were having trouble with for

You’re lucky Sojiro closed up shop early or he would’ve torn you a new one!”
“Oh come on, I almost had him that time!” Ren grumbled. “I had his patterns down, it was

“If it was a weekend, maybe, but it was a school night!” Morgana yowled. “You wanna

Ritsuka couldn’t help herself – she burst out laughing, catching the attention of the others. “II’m sorry,” she gasped through her mirth. “Just… that’s such a stupid reason Morgana has to
tell you to go to bed, Ren, you gotta admit.”
The Phantom Thief huffed indignantly. “Yes, it is a stupid reason,” he agreed, throwing a

“Oh for – you’re never going to let this go, are you?” Morgana lamented as he brought his
paws over his face.
“Nope!” he agreed cheerily.
As they all laughed, Ritsuka already began analyzing the situation in her head. They had no
idea what waited for them on the island or what dangers lurked. An artifact was certainly
there, but they didn’t have a decent way of tracking it. And assuming they wouldn’t set off
any traps approaching or taking it, they certainly would trigger any defenses immediately
after. In short, the landing and the search wouldn’t be nearly as hazardous as the escape
would be.
So how would she minimize the risks?
Ideas starting forming in her mind. ‘Hey Medea, you available?’ she asked.
There was a brief pause, then the Caster answered. ‘Occupied with a few other tasks,’ she
answered. ‘Is there something amiss?’
‘Just wanted to chat with you about a few preparations before we reach the shore,’ she
replied. ‘Mind if I workshop a few ideas with you?’
There was another brief silence, then a small pulse of affirmation. ‘Very well,’ she acceded. ‘I
shall await your company.’
Ritsuka broadly grinned. ‘Thanks Medea!’ she chirped, then withdrew mental contact.
Turning back, she noticed everyone staring at her in curiosity. “I’m just gonna hash some
things out with Medea,” the redhead explained. “Better to be safe than sorry, right?
Especially with Ren out of commission.”

Ren smirked. “I’m hurt!” he called out in mock anger. “You make it sound like I’m a reckless
idiot who gets injured all the time!”
The joke was met with flat stares from everyone, with Mash even pointedly looking away to
avoid meeting his gaze. “You are,” Ritsuka stated bluntly, causing the Phantom Thief to grin
and raise his hands in surrender. “Anyway, I’ll catch you guys in a bit – so much to do, so
little time!” With that, she marched off.
“I wonder what Ritsu has in mind,” Morgana mused, watching the girl head down the stairs
into the depths of the Hind.
“Knowing her, something effective,” Ren replied with a happy grin.
---------Ritsuka double checked her supplies. After grabbing a spare knapsack in the cargo hold, she
filled it with rations, water, a first aid kit, and other supplies. There wasn’t much – she needed
to remain nimble and be able to jettison everything at a moment’s notice – but it was better
safe than sorry. Relying on Mash to be the pack mule all the time was irresponsible and, in
her opinion, just plain rude.
As she looked over her pack, she wrestled with her decisions on what to bring or leave
behind. How did Mash always figure out what was necessary to bring? She always made it
look so easy.. Maybe she could ask for one or two packing tips, just in case…
“Is everything alright, Master?” came a familiar female voice.
“Mar-OW!” The redhead squawked as she rapidly stood up – and slammed her head against a
lower beam, causing the saint to wince in concern. “Ow ow ow,” she squeaked as she rubbed
her head. “Y-yeah, just making sure I’m good to go. How’s everyone else?”
“They’re gathered on the top deck and waiting for you,” Martha answered. “Would you like
me to take a look at that?”

The Rider nodded. Together, they made their way back up to the top deck where the others

The redhead laughed. “Always gunning for the treasure, aren’t you?” she remarked as she

“I’m sure she doesn’t mind if it helps keep us safe,” Mash reassured her with a bright smile.

Before long, they reached the surf and collided with the beach. As they hopped off, Ritsuka

“So, where are we headed?” Drake called over, her eyes already gazing into the forest

Drake nodded. “Aye, no one wants their treasures stolen,” she agreed before she grinned. “So

The sound of boots hitting the dirt announced Drake’s landing from the tree. “Nothing I can

----------The trees began thinning out, the softer natural soil yielding to harder, more compacted dirt.

Ritsuka blinked in surprise. According to Ren and Morgana, the shrine they had reached was

‘For more isolated sites of worships, yes,’ the witch confirmed as the group slowly stepped

isolated from civilization for the most part to better commune with the gods. Though there

Despite all their caution, they finally made it to the central temple without any incident.

It wasn’t long before the redhead was panting for air, her body ablaze even with the

Sparing a glance around her, it was soon clear she was the only one struggling. Neither Mash,

That was to be expected – they either had Servant physiologies in Mash’s and Joan’s cases or

“Oi, Red!”
Drake’s voice seemed to echo from far away. Blearily looking up, she blinked as the watched

The captain’s scowl deepened. She laid a heavy hand on the redhead and, before anyone

Ritsuka sighed in frustration as Mash looked over in alarm. “I’m sorry, senpai,” she quickly

The redhead’s mouth hung open in shock for a moment before rapidly shaking her head. “No,

Mash coughed as she smashed into the cliff side again, the rock yielding and crumbling
underneath her from the sheer force of the blow.
The serpent had been a formidable foe back on the ship during the storm, and it was no
different here. Just like before, the environment favored it heavily: The rocky shelf was
incredibly narrow with no easy retreat, while it could use the rapids as it pleased. Even the
less outright calamitous weather was hardly in her favor.
With a cry, Mash charged in, ducking under a claw swipe and slamming her shield against its
chest – only for her fierce blow to simply bounce off. She rolled aside as the serpent snapped

Her grieves dug into the rocky ground beneath before she managed to deflect the blow,
though it quickly dove into the rapids again before she could retaliate.
The Shielder’s grip tightened on her shield as she ground her teeth. She barely raised it in
time as its tail lashed out and struck, sending her sliding across the shelf. Was there even
anything she could do here?
Bursting out of the rapids again, the monster lunged forward with a roar. She raised her shield
again to block it – and her eyes widened in surprise as instead of the impact she expected, a

its body and flung her with great force into the middle of the rapids.
Mash felt her heart drop as she flew through the air. Crashing through a rock jutting out and
bounced back up, she winced at the impact as they exacerbated her current wounds. She

prongs. Pulling herself back in, she landed on top of its narrow surface – and almost slid from
the wet, smooth surface of the stone.

All of that was fine, it was okay. The serpent’s agility was terrifying, almost as much as its

If push came to shove, if nothing else mattered, would you use that shield to protect Mash

Focus on what you can do. You are still a strong, intelligent, capable young woman, Mash,

It should be that simple. Yet…
Everything after this, it’s all you. I’m looking forward to it, Mash.

sentimental it was to her, it wouldn’t be any help to her right now. Slowly, her grip slackened.

It's a big, wide world, Mash. Isn't there something you want to experience? Something you
want to go for?
Realization slowly trickled into the Shielder’s mind. She remembered now - being protected

However, if there is something you need – nay, you want – then you must reach out and seize
it with your own hands.
Within your grasp is a tool to assist with that.
A blaze ignited deep within Mash, filling her body with almost manic strength and heat. She

She was its enemy.

know. Just… just a little bit of help… please…?”
The Phantom Thief said nothing for a moment, watching as the two combatants stared each
other down. “I think… for the first time, this is what Mash wants,” he stated quietly. “She
knows the weight of that sword I gave her and wouldn’t have drawn it lightly. Honestly, I
don’t think she’s been any more awesome than she is now. What do you think?”
Ritsuka was at a loss for words. Ever since she arrived at Chaldea, she had stolen glances of
Mash whenever they passed by and observed her whenever they spoke. Mash had always
been cute and polite, but there was always a sense of… emptiness behind her words and eyes.
Methodical and curated, like a machine taught to interact with people. She felt more like a
doll than a person.
But now, she could see it: In Mash’s violet eyes burned a light she hadn’t seen before. She
always thought her friend and crush was awesome, but even that expectation had been blasted
straight through. Challenging an opponent without reason was something she had thought
was beyond the demure Shielder. The sword shone in the sun, highlighting her face set in
determination.
Despite how weary she seemed, with her shield and sword, facing down the serpent, she
looked every part like a hero of legend.

The redhead swallowed hard again, forcing herself to release the tension that was building up
in her shoulders. “Then… she’ll win,” she finally whispered. “She’s awesome enough for it.
She’ll win for sure. Right, Ren?”
Ren smiled warmly. “I think so too,” he agreed before keeping close watch. “She’s a lot
stronger than she thinks.”
A slow smile spread across his face as their battle cries tore through the air.
---------The flash of the blade. The tearing claws. The mass of the shield. The gnashing fangs.
Mash ducked under a tail swipe as she danced to the serpent’s side. Charging in, she raised
her sword and thrust at the open side of the creature – only for it to bounce and skate off
against the creature’s scales. Scowling, she jumped and raised her shield on reflex – just as
the monster snapped at her, knocking her clear out of its reach.
Skidding to a stop, she quickly dove aside as it pounced at her. The shield, while massive,
was like a familiar companion to her. It felt just right in her grip, like an extension of her
body. Since the Fuyuki singularity – no, earlier than that, she fought with it like she had used
it her entire life.
As the serpent whirled around, she slammed it into the ground and sprang off the top prong.
The monster rushed the embedded shield with a roar and knocked it over before halting in
confusion. Gritting her teeth, she once again summoned her shield at her feet and launched
herself down, bringing the point of her sword down on its headOnly for the tip to once again bounce off and catch on the edge of one of its scales. The
creature roared in outraged surprise and began whipping its head about. The Shielder only
had enough time to pluck the sword free before springing off, tucking herself and rolling to a
stop on the ground.
The sword, on the other hand, felt awkward and clumsy. While it felt good in her hand, she
couldn’t use it like she could the shield. She had been trying to mimic what she had seen
from Leonidas, Boudica, and the Roman soldiers, but it was nothing more than a stopgap.
Weaving her way under a claw swipe, she swiftly checked for any openings. Attacking the
maw was too risky to try again. The eyes were obvious targets, but they would be protected.
The scales were too hard for either sword or shield. There was something she missed,
somethingSuddenly, her mind flashed to when her blade caught on the scale earlier. Perhaps…
A snarl ripped her out of her rumination as a tail came smashing down. Raising her shield in
a tilt, it slid off and crashed into the ground beside her, almost knocking her aside. Steadying
herself, she lunged for the tail and wedged the sword underneath one of the scales. Stomping
on it, she pushed against the blade and levered hard.

With a horrific tearing noise, she pried some scales off the tail and exposed the soft flesh
underneath. With a roar of pain, the serpent’s tail lashed out again and bowled Mash over.
Landing on her back, her eyes widened as she saw the great body of the monster aloft and
bearing down on her.
By reflex, she summoned her shield back to her. Bracing herself behind it while having her
sword poke through one of the prongs.
The afternoon sun quickly turned into shadow as the serpent dropped like the weight of fate
itself. If this gambit didn’t pay off, she would die.
But courting death was what her senpai risked every day, wasn’t it?
The ground underneath Mash broke and yielded, grinding her into the dirt as the wind was
knocked out of her from the impact. As her shield buckled, a sharp pain lanced through her
arm as she desperately pushed back. It was likely broken, but she couldn’t afford to check. It
was fine – it was what she expected.
More importantly, clenched in a death grip was her sword, braced against the prong and
ground. It had yielded again to the serpent’s scales, but not wholly – it was still sticking
upward. Pushing up, she quickly noticed resistance of flesh against the blade and the warmth
dripping down onto her hand.
Pressing her opportunity, the Shielder thrust upward with a loud cry and was rewarded with
another agonized roar. The monster flung itself off her, nearly tearing the sword out of her
grip as it ripped out of its belly. Crashing down nearby, blood spilled out of its agape maw as
it glared down at her in renewed rage.
Mash met its gaze with a steely one of her own. As she tightened the grips of her shield with
her sword hand, pain pierced through her body and caused her to wince slightly. The shield
would brace her arm, but she couldn’t unsummon it anymore. That cut down on her options.
Blood dripped down from her blade. She wouldn’t get another opening like that again, so she
tossed away all notions of defense and caution.
Tensing her legs, the Shielder charged again, dashing straight for the monster. With a snarl,
the creature slammed a claw down on her, forcing her to sidestep. Taking advantage of the
opening, she quickly leaped on top of it and jumped up, swinging her shield outward at its
head. It collided hard with its skull, but it simply shook her away, throwing her aloft once
again – toward its tail.
Twisting in midair, she raised her blade and aimed carefully until she found what she was
looking for: The tiny spot where she had pried the scales off the serpent, exposing a spot of
flesh. She came down swiftly, the tip of her sword gleaming eagerly like a meteorThe tail suddenly whipped about as the serpent spun, and instead it began speeding straight
toward her. Her eyes widening, she swiftly raised her shield again just as it slammed into her,
sending a fresh jolt of excruciating pain through her body. Carried along by the appendage,
she clung on for dear life as she sought out the spot once more.

The singular moment stretched into what felt like hours, battered and dragged through the
pain. But with her eyes straining to focus, she caught it – a clear patch of fleshy pink and red
among the sea of blue-green scales – and she began crawling agonizingly towards it.
The edges of the scale cut into her palm, causing them to bleed. Each flick of the tail caused
her brain to rattle within her skull and her vision to darken, yet still she wasn’t deterred.
The serpent, in contrast, became more frenetic. With an almost fearful snarl, it jumped and
lashed about, desperately trying to dislodge the Shielder. Slamming its tail against the ground
and dragging it along the rocks, the monster snapped and flailed, roaring and smashing her
over and over against stones and trees.
Yet no matter what, Mash clung on more persistently than any gnat. Her body bruised, cuts
tearing open, and when she was battered against the stone her armed screamed to her through
the agony. But she held on, and nothing this creature could ever do would make her let go.
With a bloody crawl, she reached the weak spot. Raising her sword, she brought the point
down with a fierce cry while letting go of the tail. The blade pierced deep into the flesh as her
weight brought it down with her, sending them both crashing to the ground.
The creature’s screech reverberated through the air, but she wasn’t done. Raising her shield,
she hammered down on the pommel of the blade. The force of it pierced through the other
side of the tail and into the ground below, nailing it in place. Her arm throbbed but she
disregarded it as feverish energy rushed through her body.
She had her opening.
The Shielder sprang up on the pommel of the sword and quickly ran up the serpent’s back as
it struggled to pull itself free, snarling in desperation and no small amount of fear. She
pounced at its head, slamming her shield down on top with all her might.
The monster reeled from the blow but slowly began to stand back up, dazed. Without
hesitation, she furiously and unrelentingly smashed down on its skull over and over. The rock
beneath its head cracked from the brutal, thunderous impacts until its legs finally gave out,
sending it sprawling. It let out a low growl as more blood spilled out of its great maw, its
great vigor spent.
Mash held out her hand and without thinking or realizing, her sword flashed back into her
hand. Hopping off the side, she let out another wild cry as her blade pierced through a great,
baleful eye. The serpent shrieked in agony and rage, its head and body helplessly dragged
with Mash as she dropped to the ground.
Releasing the blade, she spun around and crouched. Grabbing hold of her shield in both
hands, she leaped and delivered a powerful uppercut underneath its jaw. The sheer might of
the Shielder and the monster’s own exhaustion caused it to flop over with a snarl of agony,
crashing on its side.
However, she could not – would not – relent.

Landing on the ground, she rammed it hard in the belly where she had pierced through
moments earlier. Again, the serpent roared out and tried to roll away from its assailant.
Mash sprang up while it was on its back and seized her shield, the straps becoming undone
by her will. With a wild cry, she slammed it down on its neck, the prongs digging into the
ground and anchoring it in place.
As the serpent desperately flailed about to free itself, the Shielder reached out and summoned
the sword to her again. Her arm dangled at her side, but that didn’t matter. Even if all her
limbs were broken, she would see this through.
Hopping up onto its neck again, she stabbed between the scales into the flesh underneath.
The monster’s snarls became more desperate, the note of panic clear in its growls. It thrashed
even harder, trying to dislodge the shield as its stubby claws tore up the ground underneath,
unable to reach her. Yet no matter how much it bucked about, Mash wouldn’t be dislodged.
The Shielder threw her weight behind the sword as she had done countless times with her
shield. The blade slowly sank into flesh, piercing through hide, tendon, and muscle. Gritting
her teeth, she hammered the guard with a fist, driving it deeper and deeper into its throat until
it was completely buried within.
Seizing hold of the sword’s grip, she once against jumped off the side while dragging the
blade down with her. Pulled through by the entirety of her weight and might, it cut through
the serpent’s neck and sliced it wide open. Landing on the ground, she stumbled slightly, then
let out a roar cry as she tore the blade out.
A screech, piercing and shrill, blasted from the serpent. As it thrashed about in its death
throes, blood fountained into the air and rained down, splattering her in crimson and forcing
her to shield her eyes. Eventually, its movements diminished, becoming weaker and weaker.
Then eventually it fell still, its remaining eye going dark and glassy, and moved no more.
Mash stared blankly at the monster, now dead at her feet. Though she kept her guard up, a
quick observation showed the truth, plain as day. It was dead. She had won.
The Shielder slowly let out a ragged breath. Despite her exhaustion, she felt oddly light on
her feet. When she managed to win in previous battles, all she had felt was relief and pride –
not in herself, but in Ren-senpai and their companions. The sensation was no substitute for
actual energy, but it buoyed her up and kept her standing, if only for a bit longer.
Looking down at her blade, she noticed the sword was utterly soaked in blood. Mash couldn’t
help but frown in concern. She needed to wash and maintain it. It wouldn’t be right to leave
senpai’s gift so dirty. And she needed a wash herself. There was so much she needed to do,
but at least she was done. She began slowly turning, then tripped over her feet and began
falling“Gotcha.”
The Shielder’s eyes widened in surprise as she looked up – and there was Ren, smiling
warmly down at her. Her mouth worked as thousands of questions flooded her exhaustion-

addled mind, each more important than the last. Yet as her vision swam, they all seemed so
irrelevant.
Instead, one simple phrase surfaced to the forefront of her mind. “I did it, senpai,” she
murmured with a dazed smile.
The Phantom Thief’s grin widened. “I saw,” he acknowledged, as he pulled her into a hug.
“You did great, Mash. I’m proud of you.” The girl smiled back, radiant and relieved, as her
eyes slowly closed. “Pixie,” Ren murmured. The fairy persona appeared in a flash of blue
flame and pointed to Mash. Her body began emitting a green glow as her injuries began
healing up.
“She’s okay, right?” Ritsuka slowly asked, eyeing her with concern.
“Exhaustion, most likely,” Siegfried diagnosed as he looked over. “While Master Ren has
healed her, it doesn’t restore spent stamina. She simply needs rest.”
“Heh, a shame she ain’t a drinker – I’d raise a flagon in her name for the show,” Drake
remarked with a broad grin as she looked over the serpent. “But we got the treasure and a
helluva tale. I’d call it a good day! Now, let’s get back to the ship! Sun’s setting and we need
to celebrate!”
Martha looked over. “Would you like me to carry her, Master?” she offered.
Ren paused, then nodded. “Thanks,” he replied. “I’d do it myself but, uh… still kinda shaky
on my feet.” He could feel his legs starting to buckle from the Shielder’s weight. Despite

The Rider gave an amused smile. “I understand,” she said, reaching over and picking up
Mash in her arms with no more effort than cradling a child. With that, they began making
their way toward the shore.
Joan had been last to leave. Staring hard at the corpse of the serpent, countless thoughts
flitted through her mind. Answers to questions and questions to answers, all murky and
unclear. What she had seen, what she felt… there was no way for her to put it into words. The
only thing that remained was a frustration that boiled over deep in her heart.
“Damnit,” she muttered before leaving to catch up with the others.

New dangers, new friends.

Romani leaned back in his chair with a heavy sigh.
It was the day after the disastrous expedition for the second artifact. Things had been beyond
frantic: Ritsuka and Mash both going missing, leaving everyone scrambling to find them,
only for them to show up a good distance away, where they had been attacked by a serpent
the entire time – the self-same serpent as the one that had harassed them back in the storm.
The doctor had been beside himself with worry. He had been monitoring their vitals like a
hawk, gauging their readings for any clue as to their circumstances. Stress levels,
introduction of foreign substances or pathogens, anything. They ultimately proved unhelpful,
and they were only found once Ritsuka finally managed to get into contact with everyone.
The bedraggled, soaked appearance of the girl and the absolute terror in her expression sent
cold chills down his spine, and the pit in his stomach grew even further when she reported
Mash was in trouble. If he could leap through the monitors to join them in the singularity, he
would have. As it was, all he could do was watch anxiously.
His fingers rapped on his coffee mug as he stared up at the ceiling. He never spoke much
with the girl before everything happened, admittedly. He didn’t recall anything particular
about her in her checkups save her rather high rayshift compatibility. While they saw each
other a couple times, they never had much reason to talk.
Then Olga suddenly announced Ritsuka was to be added to Team A, catching everyone off
guard. He certainly hadn’t expected that and didn’t even have time to do a last checkup. From
what he saw, she seemed just as surprised, but equal parts nervous and excited to be added.
He recalled applauding politely yet happily for her.
Roman glanced over at the monitor again as it showed her vitals. While her readings were
normal, her heartbeat was rapid and her stress levels were concerningly high. Reaching over
to his keyboard, he took a few notes for their next checkup and session when she returned.
He couldn’t help but wonder if the director had saved her from the bombing only to doom her
to a mission that was much greater than she had been prepared for.

“Up already, Romani?”
The doctor started in surprise as Da Vinci stepped over, her ever-present smile warm yet
teasing as she bore a plate of food. “I had thought you would still be asleep at this time,” she

He chuckled ruefully. “It was tempting,” he admitted. “But there’s still a lot to do. Ren

The genius nodded in understanding. “Both the ragazza and dear Mash certainly have been
through quite a bit,” she agreed as she set the doctor’s breakfast beside him. “That serpent
was rather tenace from what I’ve seen.”
Roman quietly nodded. They had watched the fight between Mash and the serpent. He almost
screamed at them when the group didn’t jump in to help, with only the Caster stopping him

how easily it had dealt with Mash then. She shouldn’t have been able to defeat it.
And yet, he watched with amazement as the Shielder fought with a ferocity he hadn’t seen
from her before. To pick a fight like that was irrational, something Mash would’ve learned
and trained all her life to avoid. Yet she had done so anyway and, despite all evidence she
should have lost, somehow emerged victorious.
He couldn’t help but think back to that little girl, dressed in just a lab gown, sitting on the bed
and staring up at him with blank eyes. Someone so utterly innocent, human yet inhuman,
lacking even the tiniest bit of agency for herself. Had she truly grown so much when he
hadn’t been looking?
The doctor couldn’t help but feel the tiniest bit proud yet conflicted by the realization.
Suddenly the main monitor flickered and sprung to life as the smiling face of Ren appeared.
“Morning, doc,” he cheerfully greeted. “Morning, Da Vinci.”

one of the sapphire eyes of the hippocampus and observed carefully as the gem began
glowing.
How long had it been since she had communed with the gods? Calling upon their authorities
for her magecraft was one thing, but directly contacting them was another. Even as a student
of Hecate and her wealth of power, she was leery of doing so. They too often brought
prosperity or ruin at a mere whim of theirs.

Her nostrils flared slightly as old memories crept in. She, of all people, knew far too well.
Still, if it was what their Masters wished, then she would fulfill her obligations. Her duty –
and what semblance of honor she had still – demanded no less.
With a wave of her hand, the artifact floated back into the formation. It shimmered and
suddenly, the lines of arcane energy became far more brilliant as the gemstone eyes shone
brightly in the dim light of the workshop. The divinity of Poseidon now resounded much
more powerfully than before.
The witch allowed herself a small smirk of satisfaction.
The skies were overcast as the ritual was set up. The Golden Hind was anchored some
distance away while the Chaldeans had rowed ashore on a landing boat. While Siegfried and
Martha set up a perimeter, the Masters went with Medea to provide whatever support was
necessary. The captain had been about to join them when the witch insisted that she stayed.
“This ritual is not meant for anyone but those absolutely necessary,” she stated bluntly. “Any
more may incur Poseidon’s wrath – and as a sailor, you know better than I what that means
for you and your crew.”
Drake hadn’t been amused by the Caster’s warning, but she nevertheless stayed aboard.
David had managed to find an island some distance away from where they had been sailing.
It was incredibly tiny, to the point where it took a mere half an hour to walk its
circumference, with its only point of interest being a plateau that rose around the center,
providing a spectacular view of the endless blue expanse of the seas.
Ren and Mash hauled the gigantic tuna the former managed to fish up. “Think Poseidon will
think like it?” he called out cheerfully, his magic circuits glowing green as he reinforced his
body to help carry the massive fish.
Medea glanced over. “It is not as grand as a beast of the depths, but given your reverence, it
shall be appreciated nevertheless,” she replied, a twinge of amusement dancing on her lips.
Both Ren and Morgana had been beside themselves with delight when they came across a
school of tuna and did everything they could to catch one – and to their credit, they both had
landed one each, with the former’s catch being the larger one by a slight margin. They
decided to offer the larger one, keeping the smaller one for themselves.
“I can’t wait for some fatty tuna~!” the catlike being cheered. His eyes were practically
gleaming in pure excitement and anticipation. “I know we shouldn’t rush this but oh man!”
“Is it really that good?” Mash inquired. “I’ve read a bit about Japanese cuisines but nothing
specific about fatty tuna.”
“Apparently it makes for really good sushi,” Ritsuka supplied with a shrug as she eyed the
tuna. While she heard tunas could be massive, actually seeing one in person compared to

herself was a different matter entirely. “I wouldn’t know though – it’s got a hefty price tag
where I’m from.”
“It’s not cheap in Japan either,” the Phantom Thief laughed. “But yeah, it’s great. The fat
makes it practically melt in your mouth. Combined with its natural umami goodness and it’s
just fantastic. I don’t think I’ll ever like it as much as Morgana, but he’s not understating how
good it is.”
As they conversed, the ritual was quickly set. With Medea’s magecraft, an altar and braziers
were crafted in the middle of a magic circle she had sketched out. The tuna was laid out on
the former as the latter were set ablaze with a whispered word from the Caster. Lifting her
staff, the artifacts and uncut gems floated in the air and blazed to life as lines of divine energy
linked them once again.
Suddenly, the sound of wind became muted. In contrast, the crashing waves on the shore
below increased in intensity, albeit they seemed almost distant and echoed all around them.
The magic circle began glowing faintly at first with a deep, shimmering blue, and steadily
brightened. The light seared into their eyes, making it difficult to see as the others stood back.
Yet throughout it all, the witch was unmoved. “Poseidon, hear your humble servant,” she
chanted, dropping into the tongue of gods and divinity. “Accept this offering as I beseech
your presence and beg for an audience.”
Raising her staff, the tuna floated into the air and began lowering into the brazier. As soon as
the flames touched it, they immediately turned azure blue. The offering dissolved into ashes
almost immediately yet instead of smoke, sea spray suffused into the air, its scent far more
overpowering and intense than anything they had experienced while sailing.
The formation above the altar glowed even more brightly and seawater began coalescing
around it. It flowed and shifted, mercurial and temperamental. Medea’s expression didn’t
change as an overwhelming – yet familiar – presence made itself known. It filled the area
around her, bearing down with its sheer power and might. Yet still she stood undaunted.
Flashes of visions flowed through her mind – the tranquil open waters, waves crashing on
rocks, the lashing storms and winds. She blinked, and she saw schools of fish flitting through
sunlit waters, predators gliding and cutting through the oceans, scavengers prowling the
shoals and reefs, and unknown leviathans ponderously floating through the dark depths.
Then it all faded away, and the witch once more was standing in the glowing circle. The
presence was still there, vast and powerful. She could feel her heart hammering hard against
her ribs as terror and awe filled every fiber of her being. Despite having done this several
times, it was something she could never get used to.
Still, she discarded the thought. He heard her prayer and accepted her offering. He was
listening.
‘My lord, there is an isle here that lies under your protection,’ she silently prayed. ‘Your
humble servant wishes to access it, so that we may inquire to the truths within and set right
the natural order of the world and restore your dominion.’

The waters that pooled around the formation shifted more intensely, their splashes echoing
like the crashes of myriad spears. Medea could feel her robes being pulled to and fro, as
though they were being battered by an ocean current. The air around her seemed to darken,
though whether in anger or consideration she didn’t dare to guess.
Her vision flashed again. She beheld a great storm as the Golden Hind sailed toward a great
being made of water, Drake at the prow roaring and laughing through the sheets of rain with
her pistols drawn. The ridiculous sight almost caused the witch to lapse in her focus, yet there
was no mistaking it: the captain had fought against Poseidon, and it was clear he hadn’t
forgotten that.
Then the sky cleared up and she was suddenly hurtled across the open waters at a dizzying
speed. A vast island now lay before her, much akin to the other ones they had explored. Then
she thrown forward and into a hole leading underground. Speeding through, the Caster
watched the rough cave walls turning into carved blocks as she was dragged through
countless turns and twists.
Finally, she saw two beings, cast in shadow. One was much larger than the other, almost
dwarfing it in comparison. It turned toward the hurtling Medea and rushed toward her, its
ravenous maw opening to consume her wholeAnd suddenly, she was back in the circle again. Taking a shaky breath, she could feel the
beads of sweat gathering on her forehead and tracing down her neck. Visions from the gods
were rarely so obvious, yet this one was perhaps the clearest one she had seen even when she
had been alive. It still left her with questions, yet she couldn’t ask. Not without the possibility
of annoying the god.
‘Your will be done, my lord,’ she whispered, lowering her head in supplication. ‘Will you
guide us to our destination?’
The air shifted again, almost lightening at the question. A single uncut gem floated free from
the formation and began glowing. It morphed as it slowly floated downward until it finally
rested on the altar, as though in invitation.
Medea slowly approached and gently picked it up. The uncut gem was now a perfect sphere,
small enough to fit in the palm of her hand. It was transparent, showing it was completely
filled with seawater. Within a shimmering emerald horse floated in the center, unmoved by
gravity. Tilting it slightly, she observed the horse face the same direction regardless of
movement and immediately gleaned the tool’s purpose.
Once more she bowed her head. ‘My thanks, lord Poseidon,’ she whispered. ‘We shall set
forth with all speed and fulfill your bidding.’ The air lightened further, as though the presence
was satisfied with her obeisance.
The formation slowly lowered back down onto the altar as the presence’s power dwindled.
The seawater enveloping it splashed away as the glow faded, leaving the rest of the uncut
gems and the two artifacts laying innocuously on the platform. The magical energy of the
circle ebbed away, leaving behind nothing but the carvings. The azure flames flickered, then
turned a bright orange once again.

And in a moment, it was gone. The sound of waves was distant again, far below the hill, as a
breeze whistled through. Medea surreptitiously reached up and wiped away the sweat. That
had gone far better than she had expected. Good.
“So, I’m guessing we got what we needed?”
The witch looked up to see her Masters warily approaching. Ren’s eyes were red as he
scanned the area – most likely seeking out any traces of the god remaining, corporeal or
incorporeal. “We have,” she confirmed, holding up the compass. “This shall lead us to our
destination. However, be aware that our trials are not yet over.”
“Nothing’s ever easy with Greek gods, is it?” Ritsuka sighed. “Was Poseidon at least a bit
more forthcoming or helpful than Artemis?”
Medea’s lips curled in a humorless smile. “It is rare that the gods are straightforward – and
this proves to be no exception,” she stated. “The bounded field protects a great island and
residing within are two beings who may prove hostile to us. We are to make our way there
and deal with them as necessary.”
“Sounds easy,” Morgana mused, crossing his paws. “Too easy. Anything about the Grail?”
“No, nor did I deem it a suitable time to ask,” the Caster replied, her eyes flicking over to the
catlike being underneath her hood. “There was much risk he would turn his wrath on us
should I press for information. It would’ve been unwise, to put it bluntly.”
“Well, we do have a habit of annoying gods,” Ren remarked with a grin as his eyes returned
to normal. “If everything’s settled, then we should get back to the ship. We got a destination
and a meal to prep – a productive day, if you ask me.”
Morgana’s eyes widened. “The fatty tuna!” he cried. “Come on, we gotta go! If it goes bad
before I get even a single slice, I’m going to take it out on all of you!”
The Phantom Thief laughed at his best friend’s insatiable hunger. “We definitely don’t want
that,” he agreed before following him down the hill.
Ritsuka turned back to Medea. “Anything else we need to do here? Cleanup or follow-ups?”
she asked. “Or are we good to go?”
Medea stared at the redhead for a moment, then shook her head. “The ritual is finished, nor is
there anything else that needs to be done save for cleaning,” she answered. With a wave of
her hand, the braziers extinguished themselves and the soot dissipated, followed by a fresh
wind that blew away any dirt and dust that had gotten in.
She decided not to disassemble the altar. An extra bit of flattery and reverence toward
Poseidon never hurt.
The girl raised an eyebrow at the spell making quick work of said cleaning. “Huh,” she
grunted. “Sounds good to me. Come on, let’s hurry back to the ship before the others devour
the tuna.”

“Of course,” Medea agreed. She watched as Ritsuka turned to leave. The girl’s eyes had
become… dull since the other day. Her children had similar ones before: Despondency over
their failures, accompanied by brooding and sulking. It seemed her expedition weighed
heavily on her Master despite her preparations and all due caution.
She shook her head. The girl truly was inexperienced compared to the other Masters. It
would almost be adorable in its childishness if it didn’t pose a liability to their mission.
Still, she dismissed the thought from her mind as she made her way down as well. That
wasn’t her problem. If she ultimately proved to be unreliable and a hindrance, then the other
Masters simply needed to pick up the slack. They couldn’t afford to coddle her, not at this
crucial juncture, and she had no desire to either.
And besides, as the Golden Hind came into view once again, she had other issues that needed
to be addressed.
“Huh. Had a hunch but wasn’t sure that was the case.”
The captain’s cabin was rather crowded – Drake sat at the head of the table while the
Chaldeans had taken the other seats. A large platter was set out in the center, with the tuna
sliced up into sashimi carefully and tastefully arranged on top. Despite the large crowd, there
was more than enough for everyone.
“Indeed,” Medea replied. “Poseidon has not forgotten your defiance or the Grail you had
taken from him. It is fortunate that he has not visited greater retribution on you and yours.”
Drake grinned broadly. “Let him try,” she boomed. “Sounds like a helluva adventure to me!
And if he’s hoarding even more loot as good as the Grail here, then all the better!” She

somehow mastered about a minute after learning of their existence) and gulped it down with

“Maybe that wouldn’t be wise,” Mash pointed out nervously. “Directly challenging a Greek
god always led to severe consequences for everyone involved. Perhaps, as a sailor, it would
be better to venerate him a bit more…?”
“What, don’t tell me you’re turning lily-livered now,” the captain guffawed. “And here I
thought you might’ve showed a bit more pluck after yesterday, o’ mighty serpent strangler!”
The Shielder squeaked as Ritsuka choked on her rice. “Pl-please don’t call me that!” she
yelped. “I-I merely managed to slay it, n-nothing more! And certainly not b-by
strangulation!”
“Aye, whatever you say, serpent strangler,” Drake remarked, her grin unwavering. The
nickname was already making its rounds around the crew and nobody hesitated to call her
that, much to the Shielder’s embarrassment.

Ren, who was smiling with amusement, glanced over to Medea and mentally connected with
her. ‘So do we have to be wary of Poseidon, then?’ he asked. ‘I don’t think you told the
captain the full story.’
‘I didn’t,’ the Caster confirmed. ‘We are well past the Age of the Gods. He would have long
since retreated to the Reverse Side of the World at this point. What we have encountered are
merely echoes and lingering aspects he can connect to, no more. The risk he poses now is…
far less than during my time.’
‘Good to know,’ Ren mused, thoughtfully munching on a slice of sashimi. ‘But I’m guessing
you want us to keep our guard up regardless?’
‘I need not remind you again the spitefulness of the gods,’ she admonished, a note of
impatience creeping in her voice. ‘His power may have considerably waned, but he can still
interfere at the most inopportune moment. Being so flippant will only make things more
difficult.’
‘Duly noted,’ Ren casually replied, sensing the witch’s irritation increase further. “I’m kind of
surprised we’re having this tuna all to ourselves,” he remarked out loud. “Pretty sure there’s

“Most sailors can’t stomach raw fish,” Drake pointed out. “Lotta worms and other parasites

just about nothin’ else.”
“It’s true,” Siegfried remarked. “I have had companions who have eaten undercooked fish

in acknowledgement.
“Aye,” the captain agreed with an amused grin. “They’d turn their nose up to this feast, which
means more for us!” She laughed loudly as she tipped her chair back and raised her goblet of
wine. “To you and your foreign cuisine! May the boys always leave it for us to enjoy!” With

Morgana, meanwhile, was sitting on the table, happily eating his slices of sashimi. Taking his
time savoring each one, he held onto his cheeks as he meowed his bliss. “Oh, fatty tuna~” he
breathed. “How I missed you! It’s been so long~! And it’s so fresh too! I don’t think we’ve
had anything like this in Japan!”
Despite her moodiness, Ritsuka managed to smile a bit in amusement. “I think you’re
blushing,” she pointed out. “I didn’t even think cats could blush. It’s really that good, huh?”
“How couldn’t I?! This is divine!” he cried as he finally gulped down his current mouthful.
“You see what I mean, right?!”
The redhead pursed her lips, then shrugged. “It’s alright,” she honestly stated. “I think it’d be
better if there was soy sauce or wasabi though.”

The catlike being froze in the middle of grabbing yet another slice, then slowly turned toward
Ritsuka as the air around him suddenly turned colder. “What did you say?” he whispered.

“I know,” Morgana replied curtly. “Which is why I’m not immediately accusing you of being
so uncultured. I’m going to teach you the finer points of how to appreciate fatty tuna, and you

Further down the table, away from the rest of the table as they laughed in amusement, Joan

Abruptly she stood up. “Not much of an appetite,” she stated simply without bothering to
look at them. “Thank you for the food. I’ll go keep watch on deck.”
Without waiting for a response or answer, she stalked out of the captain’s cabin. The cool

nauseating, her senses sharpening from the threat associated with the ocean.
The Lancer huffed as she walked down the deck. Not like she would ever get used to the sea.
The sound of footsteps approaching from behind her, soft yet deliberate on the deck, alerted

“Oh, um… I just wanted to see how you were.”
Joan turned in surprise at the stammered answer to face Mash. “It’s not like you to simply

The Shielder smiled ruefully. “Yes, but truth be told there is still a lot of fish,” she admitted.
“I do believe we will need your assistance to finish them all.”
The Lancer couldn’t help but chuckle a bit. “What, so between Ren, Siegfried, and the

Mash immediately flushed in embarrassment. “W-well, it was, um, just, um…!” she
immediately stammered. Joan’s grin widened at the reaction. She understood a bit better why
Ren and Loki liked to tease people so much - the reaction was rather amusing.

Finally, she sighed in defeat. “I simply wished to see how you were doing,” she confessed.
“Though perhaps I’m overstepping my boundaries…?”
The amusement quickly faded from the Lancer’s face. “That right?” she muttered, running a
hand through her hair. Annoyance seeped into her mind. The Shielder had been taking on
more and more aspects of Amamiya, it seemed – including being nosy. Was she not entitled

drive her awayThen she stopped as Mash’s fight the other day flashed in her mind. The very reason for her
current thoughts was right in front of her. How did this innocent girl change so much in the

Joan’s gaze traveled to the girl’s waist, where her sword used to hang in its scabbard. Was
this Amamiya’s work yet again?
She looked out over the sea, organizing her thoughts. There were many questions she wanted
to ask, each one feeling just as relevant as the last. But one question swiftly overtook the

“Why did you do it?”
Mash blinked several times. “Pardon?” she inquired.
“Why did you fight the serpent?” the Lancer repeated without turning toward her. “You know
damn well you had no chance against it. Back on the ship, I couldn’t even make a damn

Finally, she turned and stared the Shielder directly in the eye. “Running would’ve been smart.
Holding out I can understand,” she continued. “So why did you fight? Was it something in

“Stop.”
Joan paused, the pointedness in the unassuming girl cutting her off. “Please, don’t speak

The clear edge in the Shielder’s tone took the Lancer aback. “…fine, it’s not that,” Joan

Mash didn’t immediately answer. Holding out her hand, the sword appeared in her palm as

The Lancer frowned as she crossed her arms, observing the sun shining off the blade. No,

What was she missing?
“So did you find it?” Joan suddenly asked. “What you wanted? You drew the blade for a

For a moment, Mash didn’t answer as she stared at the sword contemplatively. “I… I think

Joan stared wordlessly at Mash. “… that’s it?” she inquired. “That’s… that’s all you wanted?

Mash frowned slightly in thought as her sword vanished in her hands. “It’s a rather simple

After the Shielder went back to the captain’s cabin, Joan was once more left on the prow by

moment, but it nevertheless rolled in her mind. Was it ultimately that simple?
Shaking her head, she got up and began making her way back. Perhaps she should take her
own advice after all.
Guided by Poseidon’s compass, the voyage had been relatively uneventful. The seas were
smooth and calm, with only a few clouds in the sky. According to David, the horizon was
clear as far as he could see, with nothing untoward either natural or unnatural approaching.
Nothing beset them except perhaps the tediousness of boredom.
Then, as they were sailing across what seemed to be a stretch of open water, a mist suddenly
lifted up from nowhere and shrouded everything from view. They could barely see anything
in front of their eyes. “Man the guns, every hand stay at two abreast!” Drake called out,
pulling out her pistol as she warily looked about.

“I’m guessing this is the bounded field,” Ren commented lightly as he drew his own gun.
Medea, who stood beside the helmsman, nodded tersely. “Undoubtedly,” she murmured. In
the silence of the mist, even her whisper felt far too loud. “While Poseidon isn’t known for
subtlety, he could be tricky from time to time. Be wary of anything.”
The ship sailed on in silence. In the distance, they could all hear great splashes of water and
the cries of unseen sea creatures. Each time they tensed up, their grips on their weapons
tightening. Ren quietly watched the mist with his Third Eye while Medea scanned the area
around them for any threats.
Then just as quickly as it arrived, the mist suddenly fell away and vanished - and now in front
of them was the great island Medea had been shown. It was much like the others, save for the
size: Sandy coast that became rocky shoals and rising into cliffs, forests beyond that slowly
ascended into hills. There was no sign of any monsters – though it was likely they simply hid
in their lairs.
“Right, stay on your toes!” Drake called out as she stowed away her pistol. “Don’t want
anything ambushing us from behind!”
“Aye aye!” the crew chorused as they returned to their tasks, though they kept a watchful eye
on the surrounding waters.
The Chaldeans meanwhile quickly decided who was to be sent on this expedition. Once
more, the Caster would be remaining on the Golden Hind to maintain its protections as well
as monitor the situation. Martha was also staying with Tarrasque patrolling the waters
underneath the ship; the mist had made everyone uneasy about possible hostile sea creatures.
For the Masters, Ritsuka volunteered to stay behind. “I’m not really up for being
underground again. My hands are still shaking,” she explained with a rueful laugh, showing
them to emphasize her point. “I’ll keep Martha and Medea topped up and stay in contact with
Chaldea. They probably had enough scares yesterday, I think.”
“Yeah, I get that,” Morgana replied, nodding sympathetically. “Take it easy today, Ritsuka.

‘Communications stable,’ the Caster replied. Ren glanced over to Morgana, who had a silver

Though even in the far more likely case she was lying, well…

The bake-kujira was worse.

“Masks of my rage,” he growled. “Become my wings of rebellion!”

For Morgana, the Minotaur had always been depicted as a literal bull-headed monster with a

he called his friends and comrades: Determination, and not for himself.

Ren had to admit, this was more fun than he expected.
He hadn’t thought he’d be facing off another group by himself so soon after the Roman
singularity. The pounding rain and slick mud, the eyeless faces of the silent artificial soldiers,
Leonidas watching carefully in the background… while he started with his usual flare, it had
ground him down from a Phantom Thief into desperately scrabbling for the last few kills.
It had also thrilled him in a way he hadn’t expected before. Facing off against a whole host,
pushing himself until every last bit of his energy was spent, the primal rawness that came
from utterly exhausting himself. While similar situations happened back in his Metaverse
adventures, doing so in reality was even more exhilarating.
The Phantom Thief wove through the horde, his new cloak whipping around him like his old
coat as he dispatched the monsters. A rushing wolfman was met with a bullet between the
eyes while another was sliced vertically as he backflipped away. He slid under a salvo of
energy blasts and smirked at the snarling lamia before firing his pistol – a shot to the chest
followed by one to the head.
Using the Jeanne d’Arc persona had been a stroke of lucky genius on his part. Many of the
attacks aimed at him veered away at the last moment due to its power, and the few that got
through were negated anyway. It allowed him to fight far more recklessly, closer to how he
used to fight. After being stuck on the back lines for so long, this was liberating.
A sharp sting from the cut on his cheek reined in his most bombastic impulses, however. The
protection wasn’t foolproof: a chance attack could still make its way through and he couldn’t
afford to dispel his cloak to call up another persona for healing. The circuits burning within
his flesh maintained his reinforcement, bolstering his speed and strength.
Ducking underneath a pouncing chimera, he rushed in to gut another wolfman. The longer
this went, the worse things would turn out for him. He needed to find Euryale and deal with
her as soon as possible. He glanced over to the manticore, who was standing nearby
growling, its spiked tail waving menacingly – and faltered as he noticed: the girl was
missing.
His attention was torn away as another chimera lunged at him. ‘Medea, how are the others?’
he panted out, unable to conceal his rapidly building exhaustion despite his exhilaration. ‘Are

we making any headway?’
‘The others are faring better than you are,’ Medea quickly replied. ‘Withdraw as soon as
possible. I’ll see what I can do to guide you out.’
‘Working on it,’ he chuckled as he fired at an energy blast headed his way, causing it to
explode in midair. She was right; although he was managing right now, it won’t last much
longer.
Finally, as he somersaulted over yet another chimera, a way out cleared. It was further down
the corridor, leading away from the horde of monsters and the manticore. He would have to
deal with Euryale later. For now, he tensed his legs, then sprinted for the opening towards
escape“Leaving so soon~?”
Ren’s eyes widened as Euryale suddenly appeared right beside him with a smirk. Before he
could react, she pressed a pair of fingers to her lips and blew a kiss his way.
And all at once, his mind went blank.
Why was he running again…?
Why would he ever want to run…?
After all, his idol and goddess was right here in front of him…
Euryale’s cruel smirk filled his half-lidded eyes, and it was the most beautiful sight he’d ever
seen. A dopey smile carved its way across his face, though he could faintly hear Medea
yelling at him through his cuff, he ignored it.
She didn’t matter. Nothing mattered. As he slowly reached out his hand towards her, he knew.
Only the being in front of him was worthy of his attention and adoration.

“You went from desperate and fierce to slack-jawed and docile like a little rabbit. It’s kind of

Yes, he had pleased her. He would do anything to hear that again. Anything for her.

Carefully stirring the pot in a nearby campfire, Martha checked the consistency and color of

again. Perfect.

It had started as a simple thing: Drake had summoned a host of ingredients from the Grail for

Martha, concerned, approached to advise and help, but they had proven less than cooperative

The sailor nodded. “Yes, ma’am,” he acknowledged before going back to grilling.
The man’s focus and expression as he resumed cooking brought a small smile to her lips. It

fulfilled, some not, others cut short by war, plague, or famine.
She had to wonder – if given another opportunity, in another life, would this man had become

Ren stretched as he strolled through the forest, illuminated only by the moon. The air was
cool and crisp, contrasting the warmth of the Mediterranean during the day. The scent of dirt,
grass, and bark reached his nose as he breathed in. His footsteps were muffled as he stepped
through leaves and dirt, occasionally breaking a stick or two. It was quiet, with only the
breeze reaching his ears.
He smiled. His time in the field was the only time he could think of where he was fully
immersed in nature. Tokyo was too developed – even Inokashira park was surrounded by
plaster office buildings and glass structures. And his old home was more in the suburbs than
truly out in the middle of nowhere.
Looking up, he once more beheld the full tapestry of stars peeking through the canopy above.
It was becoming a more frequent sight for him nowadays, but he still marveled at them. He
would miss it when the light pollution of the city drowned it all out again.
Stepping out of the forest, he stepped out onto the beach again. He was a good distance from
the others, to the point where even the privateers’ revelry was little more than an echo. The
rhythmic crashing of the waves during the night soothed his mind, almost carrying it away
with the tide.
The Phantom Thief roused himself with a small sigh. As much as he wanted to take a nap, he
had a job to do, and there wouldn’t be a better time to do it.
Looking around, he saw a small outcropping of rocks nearby he could climb, with a flat
plateau near the top. Walking over, he easily climbed up to the top and looked around him.

Though he wasn’t high in the air, he could still see a good distance around him. A great place
to survey the stars and the sea.
He nodded in satisfaction. Reaching into a pocket, he took out a square of cloth and unfolded
it. Placing it on the rock, he smoothed it out as best he could before backing up slightly to
admire it again.
It was an elaborate star map, wrapping around in a circle with constellations drawn and
labeled. Etched in a gold circular border were various names of constellations in different
languages. It was Olga’s personal handiwork, meant to help facilitate the ritual, but the
handiwork was still gorgeous. Maybe he should ask her to teach him.
Now he took out a vial of red and gold liquid, a small square of paper, as well as a quill.
Uncorking it, he dipped the nib in the paint, opened the paper to reveal the Animusphere
magic crest, and began tracing it on the blank center of the star map. It was intricate and
detailed, but fine work like this was well within his dexterity.
Once he was done, he sketched out the far simpler design of his command seal, shaped in his
Phantom Thief mask. Despite having never done so before, it felt familiar, as though he had
drawn it thousands of times already. He finished it with a flourish, splashing ink clear from
the star mat to the rock below, and smirked in satisfaction.
Perfect.
Finally, Ren drew out one last thing from his pockets: A small, collapsible brass telescope.
Stretching it out, he placed it on the star mat right above the two sigils. He checked all the
details then nodded. Everything was in place. Now for the coup de grace.
Sitting down cross-legged in front of the star mat, he closed his eyes. It had been a while
since he had done meditation, but he mastered the art during his time in Tokyo. It was a
matter of focusing – and not simultaneously. A paradoxical act, yet one he learned well. For
now, the Phantom Thief focused on his breathing.
He breathed in.
Then he breathed out.
He breathed in.
He breathed out.
In.
Out.
In.
Out.

The gentle splashing of the waves faded from hearing. The sensation of the rock underneath
became nothing. The smell of brine and the sea no longer registered. He saw the void beyond
the darkness of his eyelids.
He was nothing. He was everything. He was part of the world. He was apart from the world.
He was above the heavens. He was below the earth. It was the past. It was the present. It was
the future. All in this one singular moment. Eternal yet fleeting.
His consciousness reached out, touching a subtle thread. A faint aria, traced by the glimmer
of starlight. It was delicate enough that it felt the slightest bit of force would shatter and spill
like a trillion sapphires.
Despite that, his tendrils of thought gently embraced it, coaxed it, brought it closer and closer
to him. From the immaterial to the material, from non-matter to matter. The journey was
endless, spanning eons upon eons. Yet neither time nor space were relevant here in this void.
All was one and one was all. So was this thread, and so were his thoughts.
The thread drew ever closer to him. It made itself known to his presence, and he welcomed it.
Knowledge of what it was filled his mind. Now he simply had to speak its name. Opening his
mouth, he bid the thread:
“Come to me, Olga Marie Asmleit Animusphere.”
There was a burst of blue flame near Ren as he drew his consciousness back to himself.
Opening his eyes as they faded, he beheld Olga standing beside him on the rock and smiled
tiredly. “Welcome back to the regular world,” he greeted.
Olga frowned slightly in thought. “I… must admit, I was skeptical you would succeed,” she

“Thought you’d be used to that by now,” the Phantom Thief chuckled. “I’m glad it worked
though. Wasn’t sure what else we could try if it didn’t.”
“I’d simply amend the ritual if it didn’t,” the attendant quietly huffed.
“Yes, of course, o’ great lord magus.”
She shot a glare at Ren and raised her hands to begin her work, turning around to look out at

And once she did, she paused.
“It’s…” She started, trailing off as her mind was swallowed in the horizon.
“…Beautiful, yeah.” Ren finished, his own mind focused entirely on her.
A breeze, flowing out from the sea. The taste of salt on her tongue. The smells of wood and
pollen and fish and life.

This wasn’t her first time in such an environment. Whether it was social outings with other
mage families, small expeditions for personal reasons, or familial projects.
But most of the time, she had been cooped up in the luxurious manor of the Animusphere
family. Chaldea’s environment was always kept at a regulated temperature while the
simulator was strictly to run tests as necessary. The Velvet Room was relaxing and
comforting, never tiring of the aria despite it being constantly sung.
A world of dreamlike sensations where everything was distantly felt, as though she was a
